Subject: Renewal: entrance window, tier shift & phased ramp proposal

Hi Daniel / Leah,

Thanks for the productive QBR last week — appreciate the clarity on your upcoming product launch and the load profile spike expected in H2. Per our conversation, I attached an updated SOW (SOW_v3.pdf) and Q3 usage summary (usage_report_q3.csv) to ground the renewal discussion.

High-level proposal we want to confirm with you before we draft an amendment:
- 3-year amendment with phased commit ramp (conservative starting baseline, stepped increases Y2/Y3)
- Entrance window: OptiScale to elect a launch window inside a 90-day "entrance window" where committed capacity begins (helps align billing to your rollout)
- Co-term: option to co-term to calendar year (Jan 1) at renewal execution or keep anniversary-based start — we can price both ways
- Auto-renew: standard 12-month auto-renew with 60-day opt-out notice; we can make exceptions for committed-capacity true-up windows

Can you confirm: (1) whether OptiScale wants co-term to calendar year, (2) target Q4 ramp multiplier (we heard ~2x peak tokens relative to current run-rate), and (3) appetite for a multi-year prepay vs monthly true-up?

If you prefer, I can sketch two priced paths (prepay discount vs flexible true-up) for you by early next week.

Cheers,

Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
1) Co-term: We prefer co-terming to our fiscal calendar (Jan 1) if the math is close; it makes internal budgeting much cleaner.
2) Ramp profile: We expect a stepped ramp: soft launch in Q1 (baseline), 1.5x in Q2, 2x-2.5x by Q4 after full rollout. We can share a forecast but want to keep a conservative committed baseline to start.
3) Auto-renew / credits: We want a fair credit mechanism for unused committed capacity in year 1 if we under-index. Also need clarity on early-exit / termination liability if product delays push launch >120 days beyond entrance window.

Attached is our standard procurement intake form (we'll send PO after commercial terms). Can you provide a sample amendment that shows the entrance window language + credit ladder?

Marissa — here's a concise approach we can propose to OptiScale. I kept the commercial levers simple so procurement can sign off quickly: 

1) Term & co-term options
   - Option A (co-term to calendar year): 3-year term starting Jan 1, 2028; Year 1 commit = 60% of forecasted peak, Year 2 = 80%, Year 3 = 100%. 5% one-time co-term discount applied to OPEX in Y1.
   - Option B (anniversary start): 3-year term from execution date; Year 1 commit = 50% baseline, Y2 = 75%, Y3 = 100%. Slightly higher unit price to compensate.

2) Entrance window language (recommended):
   - "Customer may elect an entrance window of up to 90 days from execution to declare the commit start date. If Customer delays start beyond 120 days from execution, Customer may elect a one-time deferral (max 90 days) or convert up to 30% of Year 1 committed units into credit against Year 2 true-ups."

3) Credit / refunds
   - No cash refunds. Up to 30% of unused Year 1 committed units can convert to non-expiring credit against future committed true-ups or overage. Credits are applied after Year 1 reconciliation.

4) Early-exit exposure
   - Include a scaled termination fee that decays each quarter of the first year (e.g., Q1: 75% of remaining committed value, Q2: 50%, Q3: 25%). This gives OptiScale runway without full penalty while protecting Redwood economics.

5) Burst / on-demand
   - Allow on-demand burst at 2x per-token unit price; capped monthly at 20% of committed units unless separately agreed.

I'll add a simple commit_table_v1.csv showing example numbers for a 3-year profile. If this looks good, I can draft amendment language and a pricing appendix for Marissa to send to OptiScale.

Karthik

- Entrance window: up to 90 days to declare start; delay >120 days triggers one-time deferral or conversion of up to 30% Y1 commitment into credit.
- Credits: non-cash credit applied after Y1 reconciliation; no cash refunds.
- Early-exit: scaled termination fee that declines quarterly in Y1 (details in amendment).
- Burst: on-demand available at 2x unit price, capped as proposed by Karthik.
